messages:
maria: Quick sync — we discovered an oddity in canary + smart routing. When a canary is scoped to 10% global but we have tiered routing (enterprise 0%, standard 20%, trial 50%) the console shows 10% exposure overall but fallbacks are happening disproportionately in enterprise region. Anyone seen this?

devon: @maria saw some logs earlier. Might be interaction between the per-tier override and fallback policy: if enterprise has strict latency SLOs we route to cheaper variant A, then on decode errors we fallback to B which is in a different region.

ash: Can you paste the rollout config? We might be conflating global `exposure` with per-segment weights. We currently compute actual per-tier weight = global_exposure * tier_multiplier unless a tier-specific `exposure` is set.

maria: Copy of the minimal config that triggered it:```yaml
rollout_id: canary-2026-03-17
global_exposure: 0.10
tiers:
  - name: enterprise
    multiplier: 0.0
  - name: standard
    multiplier: 2.0
  - name: trial
    multiplier: 5.0
fallback_policy:
  variant: model-v1-fallback
  max_fallbacks_per_min: 5
  route_to_same_region: false```

lee: Ah — `route_to_same_region: false` is the culprit. If fallback sends to different region and routing chooses model-v1-backup which is only in us-east, enterprise (eu-west) sees higher perceived fallback latency and some requests get re-routed via global edge which counts toward enterprise quotas in weird ways.

sam: UX note: console shows a single "exposure" number and a per-tier column for 'Actual routed %' but it doesn't show 'fallback rate by tier' yet. We should add a small sparkline + tooltip.

devon: Implementation options: 1) compute and display expected per-tier routed share after applying multipliers and rollout exposure; 2) surface fallback rate per tier and per-region; 3) expose `route_to_same_region` as checkbox with warning.

ash: Also an API shape question — should the API allow explicit per-tier exposures (overrides) or rely on multipliers? Overriding avoids ambiguity:`tiers: - name: enterprise exposure: 0.0 - name: standard exposure: 0.2 - name: trial exposure: 0.5` Then global_exposure is ignored for tiers that set `exposure`.

maria: I prefer explicit exposures for canaries. Less mental math for PMs and less surprise. But we need validation: sum of weighted exposures must remain <=1 across tiers or we cap and normalize?

devon: We currently normalize by total multiplier. If explicit exposures exist, we validate each in [0,1] and then compute per-route traffic as min(exposure, quota_allowance). Normalization for mixed configs is messy.

lee: Telemetry alert idea: emit metric `rollout.fallback.count` with tags {tier,region,variant_from,variant_to,reason}. Then set alert if fallback_rate>2% for enterprise for 10m. That will catch hidden regressions.

sam: Console addition: small `?` helper explaining ordering: global -> tier-exposure -> weights -> fallback routing. Also show simulated sample traffic breakdown for the next N requests so PMs can preview.

ash: Edge case: A-B rollouts where variant B is only in region X. If B fails in region Y, fallback goes to older variant A which is pinned to region Y, but smart routing may then pick a cheaper variant C in a third region. We should have a tiebreaker order: prefer same-region fallback, then same-tier, then cheapest.

devon: Agree. Proposed tie-breaker priority: 1) same region + same tier 2) same region 3) same tier 4) lowest latency estimate 5) lowest cost. Also add `allow_cross_region_fallback: boolean` at rollout level.

maria: Can we also ensure quota accounting is done on the original request's tenant/tier? Right now some fallbacks are attributed to the model owner region and skew billing.

lee: Yes — quota/accounting must be attributed to the original request's tenant id and tier. We'll need a small change in the routing path: carry original_tenant_id and cost_bucket in the request envelope to fallback hops.

deploy-bot: rollout canary-2026-03-17 started by ash at 1790001300

ash: I'm going to sketch API patches: - add `tiers[].exposure` (optional) - add `rollout.allow_cross_region_fallback` - add `rollout.fallback_tiebreaker` enum - telemetry: `rollout.fallback.count` with tags. I'll open a PR and include sample console mocks.

sam: Thanks — append UX mocks to the PR. Can we also add a small 'preview' button that simulates 10k requests and shows per-tier fallback counts? PMs love that.

maria: Great. One more ask: include an example of how quotas interplay with simulated preview so we don't propose impossible exposures. E.g. if enterprise quota is 0 rps for canary, preview should show 0 exposure regardless of config.

devon: ack. I'll add quota-simulation and a validation warning in the console when exposures would exceed quota.

lee: I'll wire telemetry alerts. If anyone wants to pair on the normalization math ping me.

maria: Thanks all, assigned action items: @ash PR for API patches, @devon implement routing behavior changes, @sam console previews + help text, @lee telemetry/alerts. We'll triage in next sync. :white_check_mark:
